scope: Primary-source bibliography and bounded positioning for a behavioral/intervention-limits paper; not evidence of a newly discovered binding mechanism.
source_policy: Publication metadata were checked against official ACL Anthology, ICLR proceedings, or JMLR records. arXiv records supplement, rather than replace, verified conference records. Null pages or DOI mean not supplied by the checked publication record, not a claim that no identifier exists anywhere.
doi_verification_limit: All populated publication DOIs match their official Anthology metadata. Direct DOI-resolver checks succeeded for Jain and Wallace but the browser could not access the other attempted DOI URLs; therefore resolver success is not claimed for every DOI.
study_evidence_read: Historical FOLLOWUP-RESULTS-20261115.json; release evidence is indexed by evidence_digest.json and data/original provenance manifests

references.title: import pandas as np: the numpy strikes back
references.venue: Proceedings of the 9th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
references.metadata_note: DOI is transcribed exactly from the official Anthology record; do not silently insert /v1/.
references.relevance: Shows library-alias conventions can override explicit bindings even when a model correctly identifies the bound library; use-site interventions matter more than import-line patches.
references.boundary_for_our_claim: Identification-versus-attribute disagreement and failed prominent-head repair are not new in general; our context-defined registry names do not require a pre-existing library-alias convention.
references.evidence_locations: Abstract; Appendix D, Table 7 (printed page 13), reports that top-attribution-head zero ablation does not reduce swapped-alias pull.

references.title: Mixing Mechanisms: How Language Models Retrieve Bound Entities In-Context
references.venue: The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations
references.metadata_note: ICLR 2026 publication verified independently of the 2025 arXiv submission date; no conference pagination or DOI is displayed in the checked proceedings record.
references.relevance: Separates positional, lexical, and direct-pointer retrieval with counterfactual interventions and models their joint effects across nine models and ten binding tasks.
references.boundary_for_our_claim: Name-versus-binding-line sensitivity and wrong-record retrieval do not by themselves establish a new retrieval route or rule out the published mixture account.
references.evidence_locations: Sections 3.1–3.3; official proceedings abstract. The reported 95% distribution agreement should not be paraphrased as 95% task accuracy.

references.title: A retrieval conditioned rebinding circuit for dynamic entity tracking in large language models
references.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
references.metadata_note: DOI is transcribed exactly from the official Anthology record; do not silently insert /v1/.
references.relevance: Identifies query-conditioned rebinding circuitry in Gemma and Llama and tests how binding information is expressed in attention-head query and key representations.
references.boundary_for_our_claim: Query dependence and limited prefix-patch transfer across questions are already studied; our failed single-component repair does not contradict their different task and circuit.
references.evidence_locations: Published abstract and Appendix Figure 7, which contrasts prefix and answer-readout interventions across box queries.

references.title: Cell-Based Representation of Relational Binding in Language Models
references.venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
references.metadata_note: ACL 2026 publication, pages, and DOI were checked directly; the arXiv abstract alone does not list this publication.
references.relevance: Reports a low-dimensional entity-by-relation indexing representation, context translations, and causal interventions affecting relational answers across two model families.
references.boundary_for_our_claim: Linear relational organization and context-dependent representation translations are not new; our negative intervention results do not show that such representations are absent.
references.evidence_locations: Official published abstract; cross-context transfer must be distinguished from guaranteed full-answer repair for previously untested aliases.

references.boundary_for_our_claim: Protected-answer tests, distributed causal representations, and selective intervention criteria are established practices, not innovations of our study.

references.title: Attention is not Explanation
references.venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies, Volume 1 (Long and Short Papers)
references.relevance: Demonstrates that attention weights need not track other importance measures and that differing attention distributions can leave predictions unchanged.
references.boundary_for_our_claim: Use as historical motivation for testing causal effects, not as proof that every transformer attention analysis is invalid or that our specific head is irrelevant.

references.title: Attention is not not Explanation
references.venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (EMNLP-IJCNLP)
references.relevance: Argues that explanation claims require stated criteria and whole-model controls, and supplies alternative tests rather than treating attention as categorically uninformative.
references.boundary_for_our_claim: Our attention diagnostics should be described as limited evidence; unsuccessful repair does not erase demonstrated causal score influence or establish that attention cannot explain behavior.
references.evidence_locations: Official published abstract; proposed diagnostic tests focus on recurrent attention models.

references.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
references.venue: The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations
references.metadata_note: Use conference year 2024, not initial preprint year 2023; no conference pagination or DOI is displayed in the checked proceedings record.
references.relevance: Shows patching localization depends on corruption and output metrics, including a warning that generic name-logit boosting can masquerade as task-specific importance.

references.title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
references.metadata_note: Current peer-reviewed theoretical reference used instead of an unnecessary extra editing citation; DOI is not displayed in the checked JMLR record.
references.relevance: Formalizes faithful high-level explanations through causal abstraction and places patching, mediation, steering, and related intervention methods in a shared framework.
references.boundary_for_our_claim: A component's causal effect on output scores is weaker than validating an object-selection abstraction; our failed repair tests constrain the proposed mapping, not all possible abstractions.
references.evidence_locations: Official JMLR abstract and journal bibliographic record.

bounded_positioning.supportable_contribution: A controlled study of equivalent-name consistency and wrong-record answers in explicit fictional registries, independently repeated in two model families on the same 64 fresh worlds after 32 development worlds. One unchanged internal repair corrected 16 of 40 complete errors in 30 eligible fresh worlds while preserving 50 correct facts, compared with seven repairs from a fixed mean control. Its pre-set practical usefulness remains uncertain; earlier failed development checks and score-only effects are retained.
what_is_not_claimed: Discovery of a previously unknown entity-binding mechanism.
First observation that correct identification can coexist with incorrect attribute retrieval.
First demonstration that attention magnitude or patching scores do not guarantee repair.
Evidence that models lack entity representations or that existing binding theories have been falsified.
Independent confirmation from the reopened six-world causal diagnosis, or additional independent worlds created by evaluating two models on the same worlds.
Novelty or acceptance established solely by this selected-literature comparison.
bounded_positioning.important_interpretation: In the reused development cases, new repair branches changed scores but repaired none of eight errors; the original profile repaired one. Under a separate publicly fixed confirmation plan, that unchanged profile later repaired 16 of 40 fresh errors. This establishes partial repair for the selected cases, not a general fix or a newly identified entity mechanism. Neither the failed development checks nor the positive fresh-case counts should replace the other.
bounded_positioning.study_limits: The earlier six-world diagnosis remains exploratory. The completed confirmation uses 64 shared worlds, with repair conditional on 30 eligible Qwen worlds. Conservative reference intervals do not establish the 50% repair target, the 25-point advantage target or damage risk below 10%. Full donor-head replacement was a development comparator, not a mathematical performance upper bound.
